issues.legal_issue: A suit whose plaint is returned because the original court lacked jurisdiction is instituted in the proper court only when the plaint is presented there.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance concerning immovable property and recovery of possession, but was instituted in a court that lacked jurisdiction over the property.
The plaint was ordered to be returned for presentation to the proper court and was to be presented there after proceedings in the original court had advanced.
issues.conclusion: The suit in the proper court is instituted only upon presentation of the returned plaint there; it is not a continuation of the suit in the court that lacked jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Order 7 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for return of a plaint for presentation to the proper court. Applying Amar Chand Inani v. Union of India, the Court held that where the original court lacked jurisdiction, the suit is instituted in the proper court when the plaint is presented there, not when it was first filed. Joginder Tuli v. S.L. Bhatia was distinguishable because the suit there had been properly instituted and the plaint was returned following an amendment that affected pecuniary jurisdiction. The underlying suit concerning immovable property and possession fell within Section 16(d), and Section 20 could not confer jurisdiction on a court that otherwise lacked it.

rule.if: civil_suit_for_recovery_of_immovable_property and original_court_lacked_jurisdiction and plaint_returned_for_presentation and plaint_presented_to_proper_court

predicates.civil_suit_for_recovery_of_immovable_pro: The plaintiff brought a civil suit seeking recovery of possession of immovable property.
predicates.original_court_lacked_jurisdiction: The court where the suit was first filed lacked jurisdiction over the subject matter or location of the property.
predicates.plaint_returned_for_presentation: The court ordered the plaint returned so it could be presented to a court with jurisdiction.
predicates.plaint_presented_to_proper_court: The plaintiff presented the returned plaint to a court with jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a recovery suit concerning immovable property is returned because the first court lacked jurisdiction, the suit in the proper court begins upon presentation of the plaint there.

issues.legal_issue: A court receiving a plaint returned for lack of jurisdiction cannot treat the proceedings in the original court as a transferred suit and resume the case from the stage previously reached.
material_facts: The original court lacked jurisdiction and returned the plaint for presentation to the proper court, rather than transferring the suit.
Before the return, pleadings and evidence had been completed and the matter had reached the stage of final arguments.
The applicant sought an order allowing the proper court to continue from that stage.
issues.conclusion: The proper court could not be directed to continue the suit from the stage reached in the court that lacked jurisdiction, and the application was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 24 and 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure concern transfer of suits and did not apply because this was a return of the plaint for lack of jurisdiction, not a transfer. Order 18 Rule 15 concerns a successor judge dealing with evidence recorded by a predecessor and did not apply to this situation. The Court relied on Amar Chand Inani v. Union of India in rejecting continuity between proceedings before a court without jurisdiction and proceedings after presentation of the plaint to the proper court. The request for relief under Section 151 of the Code or Article 142 of the Constitution was not granted.

rule.if: request_to_resume_at_prior_stage and original_court_lacked_jurisdiction and plaint_returned_for_presentation and proceeding_was_not_transferred

predicates.request_to_resume_at_prior_stage: A party asked the receiving court to continue the case from the stage reached in the earlier court.
predicates.original_court_lacked_jurisdiction: The court where the case was first heard lacked jurisdiction over it.
predicates.plaint_returned_for_presentation: The earlier court returned the plaint for presentation to a court with jurisdiction.
predicates.proceeding_was_not_transferred: The case reached the receiving court by presentation of a returned plaint, rather than by an order transferring the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a party seeks continuation at a prior stage after a plaint has been returned for lack of jurisdiction rather than a proceeding being transferred, the receiving court cannot resume from that stage.
